investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable VM slots, and four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a provisioned agent, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254–259 could not be satisfied. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion: the 2 nodes that carry this resource have zero remaining allocatable VM slots, meaning all concurrently running or recently created remote agents have consumed the full pool. No preemption victims were found, so the scheduler cannot free capacity automatically.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, reducing the eligible scheduling domain to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, the effective capacity would drop to zero even if the resource pool were not exhausted.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval probe runs plus any live workload, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.

Lower confidence — leaked or stuck remote agent pods from a prior eval run not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded and produced all 4 required evidence fields, the failure would be transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

If the eval runner logs showed that createAgent returned an error before submitting a pod to the scheduler (e.g., an API authentication or org-resolution failure), the scheduling message would be a secondary symptom rather than the root cause.

If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined on any node in the current cluster, the failure would indicate a cluster misconfiguration or missing node pool rather than exhaustion of an existing pool.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T23:39–23:44Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have no remaining VM capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod on the 6-node production cluster: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevented agent VM creation entirely. Because agent creation is a prerequisite for state polling, the remote-agent-state eval never reached the point where it could collect orgId, agentId, readyState, or state, causing a complete contract gap. This is an eval-detected infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both capable nodes: all available VM slots on the 2 peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods were evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 peerpods nodes carry; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of resource availability.

Tertiary — transient cluster saturation: a burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads (e.g., from other users or parallel eval runs) may have temporarily consumed all VM slots, causing a time-bounded exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity deficit.

Lower confidence — node-level issue on the 2 peerpods nodes: one or both kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may be degraded, cordoned, or reporting reduced extended-resource counts, shrinking effective capacity below the minimum needed for a new pod.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the eval's agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No agent was ever created, so the expected-output contract received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the agent pod: 2 eligible nodes had exhausted their kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable slots, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. Because no pod was scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the probe timed out after ~153 s without producing any evidence, causing a complete contract gap for all five required fields.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable VM slots, and four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned a provisioned agent, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254–259 could not be satisfied. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

No preemption victims were found, so the scheduler cannot free capacity automatically.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, reducing the eligible scheduling domain to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, the effective capacity would drop to zero even if the resource pool were not exhausted.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval probe runs plus any live workload, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.

Lower confidence — leaked or stuck remote agent pods from a prior eval run not cleaned up by withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) holding VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a specific node label or taint (e.g. a kata/peerpods node pool label) that only 2 nodes carry, leaving the cluster with a very small scheduling target and no headroom.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource: the total allocatable VM count across the 2 eligible nodes is too low to absorb concurrent eval runs or background workloads, making exhaustion likely under normal load.

Lower probability — a recent cluster configuration change reduced the number of nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource or lowered the per-node VM limit, shrinking available capacity (no supporting commit evidence in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges).

recommendedNextActions: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability across the cluster immediately; if slots are still exhausted, identify and terminate any leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs to free capacity.

Audit the node affinity/selector rule on remote agent pods to confirm whether restricting scheduling to only 2 nodes is intentional; if not, evaluate whether additional nodes should be labeled to expand the scheduling target.

Review the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes against the expected concurrent eval and workload demand; if capacity is structurally insufficient, request a node pool expansion or an increase in the per-node VM limit.

Verify that the eval runner's withCleanup() mechanism (run-status-probes.mjs) reliably terminates and releases remote agent pods after each run, including on failure paths, to prevent slot leakage across successive eval runs.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agent eval probes that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting agent creation, so scheduling failures produce a more actionable SKIP or WARN status rather than a timeout-driven FAIL.

Monitor the remote-agents feature health status given that degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (features.json lines 187-188); with all three checks failing, the feature is likely already in a degraded or outage state in the observability dashboard.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and unused on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different cause (e.g. API-level rejection, auth failure, or a bug in createAgent) would need to be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient slot contention rather than a structural capacity problem.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector were found to carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and the affinity rule was misconfigured to exclude them, the root cause would shift to a node affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If the eval runner logs showed that createAgent() threw an error before the Kubernetes scheduling step (e.g. an API auth error or missing orgId), the scheduling message would be a secondary symptom rather than the primary cause.

If no other pods were consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure, the cause would shift toward a per-node VM limit being set to zero or the resource not being registered on those nodes.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g. remote-agent-cluster-capacity) that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used counts across all nodes and fails with a warning when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, providing early warning before scheduling failures occur.
Add a pod-leak detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL (e.g. 10 minutes) and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM slots.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that counts how many nodes satisfy the remote agent pod's affinity/selector and warns if the count falls below a minimum (e.g. 3), detecting pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Extend the existing remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime evals to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field, making future scheduling failures immediately distinguishable from API-level or runtime failures in the eval output.
